summary: Marshall Islands is shown at the grain of the IMF’s Government Finance Statistics: the central government and its social security funds, 11 lines of taxes and social contributions for 2018, in USD. The largest line is personal income tax (22%), then social security contributions of employees (22%) and social security contributions of the self-employed and non-employed (19%). Taxes on goods and services (VAT, sales taxes, excises, vehicle and similar taxes) make 11% of the total and income taxes 22%; social contributions are 41%. The folio records what each line raised; it does not describe the country’s tax laws, rates or the names of its individual taxes.
structureNote: This folio is built from one source, the IMF’s Government Finance Statistics (Statement of Operations), for 2018: the IMFâ€™s general-government series equals its central-government series, so no taxes of sub-national governments are reported. Sub-national governments are not drawn: the IMF series does not report taxes for them in this year. Lines below 0.15% of the total are folded into one “small lines” core per level; lines that the IMF reports only as a parent are drawn as the parent. Rates, legal bases and the names of the individual taxes are not recorded. The IMF labels the series 2018; where the country’s fiscal year is not the calendar year, this is the fiscal year the IMF assigns to 2018. The figures are the IMF’s and have not been compared with the country’s own statistics. There is no OECD level layer for this country in the atlas.

denominators.calculation: Sum of the 11 lines drawn (USD million). The IMF reports 66.96 million for the sector; the lines drawn differ from it by 0 million (rounding between levels of the classification).
denominators.caveat: The IMF flags the figures for this year as actual. The IMF labels the series 2018; where the country’s fiscal year is not the calendar year, this is the fiscal year the IMF assigns to 2018.
